Description:
As a developer using the XMOD model-driven workflow, I need the Hero Carousel block model fully defined so that the component-definition.json, component-models.json, and component-filters.json can be generated and the block authored in Universal Editor / DA without rework.

BLOCK IDENTITY (names must match EXACTLY across markdown title, component-definition.json, and template name):
- Block title: 'Carousel'
- Block name/key: carousel
- Variant: 'carousel (hero)' for the hero/banner styling
- Kind: container (composite) + repeating item
- Model ids: container = 'carousel'; item = 'carousel-item' (must be separate models)

CONTAINER MODEL fields (carousel) - settings for the whole carousel:
- autoplay (boolean, optional, default false)
- interval (number, optional, default 5000) -> ms between slides when autoplay
- loop (boolean, optional, default true)
- showDots (boolean, optional, default true)
- showArrows (boolean, optional, default true)
- showCounter (boolean, optional, default true) -> the '1/5' indicator

ITEM MODEL fields (carousel-item) - one per slide (5 slides in design):
- backgroundImage (reference/image, REQUIRED) -> full-bleed <picture>; needs alt
- eyebrow (text, optional, hide if empty) -> Girl Scout Bold 20/24, white
- heading (text, REQUIRED, max ~80 chars) -> Girl Scout Bold 48/58, white, H2
- primaryCta (aem-content/link, optional) -> outline button, uppercase label
- secondaryCta (aem-content/link, optional) -> text link + right chevron, uppercase
- termsLink (aem-content/link, optional) -> bottom-right, Trefoil Sans 600 12/17

MODELING RULES (per xwalk requirements):
- Container model must NOT map to the repeated item; item model is mandatory and separate
- component-filters.json must allow 'carousel-item' inside 'carousel'
- Each block must have its associated _carousel.json
- Field hints required in each authored cell so parsers map correctly

Tasks:
- Define container and item field models with the fields above
- Author component-definition.json, component-models.json, component-filters.json entries
- Apply field collapsing for image+alt where relevant; group CTA fields in editor
- Provide field-hinted sample content (5 slides)
Acceptance Criteria:
- component-definition.json registers 'Carousel' with the exact title
- component-models.json defines container model 'carousel' AND separate item model 'carousel-item'
- component-filters.json allows 'carousel-item' inside the 'carousel' container
- _carousel.json present and valid
- All field types, required flags, and defaults match the model above
- Field hints present/correct in each cell; sample content validates against the UE model
- Authoring a 5-slide carousel in Universal Editor produces the expected DOM
- See docs/SDD/XMOD-Block-User-Story-Template.md for the modeling checklist

Description:

Description:
As a user relying on assistive technology, I need the Hero Carousel to be fully accessible so that I can perceive and operate all slides and controls.

Aligns with the project WCAG 2.1 AA + Section 508 requirements. Note: all slide text in the design is white over a photographic background, so a scrim/overlay is likely required to meet contrast.

Tasks:
- Add carousel pattern semantics (region with aria-label; aria-roledescription=carousel; slides as group with position labels)
- Make arrows, counter, and dots keyboard operable with visible focus
- Provide accessible names (Previous slide, Next slide, Go to slide N of 5)
- Background images: meaningful alt text; decorative use empty alt
- Announce slide changes via aria-live=polite without flooding AT
- Verify white text over image meets 4.5:1 (apply overlay/scrim if needed)
Acceptance Criteria:
- Entire carousel operable by keyboard (Tab/Enter/Space/Arrow keys)
- Visible focus indicator on arrows and dots with >=3:1 contrast
- Controls have descriptive accessible names referencing slide position
- Slide changes announced via aria-live; no keyboard trap
- White text over background passes 4.5:1 (scrim applied as needed)
- axe-core scan returns zero violations on a page with the block
